Right—that makes the persona part of the thread’s identity. If it’s loaded into the system message at the start of the chat, the thread’s name and icon can represent that persona consistently. Persona buttons can start the right kind of chat, and the selected persona’s front matter supplies its name and icon.

That makes the thread itself the lightweight process definition: a normal chat thread, with optional automation, a chosen folder, and a pin. A small automation marker tells you it has scheduled runs; a user-chosen icon and name make pinned processes easy to recognize. Overriding the default tab lets a thread open directly into its policy or automation controls when that’s the most useful starting point.

The persona buttons fit as another layer of thread metadata. A user can choose a prompt/persona from the chat, and its front matter can supply the matching icon and persona details. I’d keep the **thread’s icon** distinct from the **currently selected persona** when a thread can use several personas, so the process stays recognizable even as its active prompt changes.

It’s a nice “ordinary thread with useful affordances” direction: pin the processes you care about, see which ones run automatically, and give each one the controls and identity that fit its job.
